source.basis: Operator spec page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
CyrusOne's San Antonio campus publishes 36 MW of IT capacity across 295,785 square feet, one of only 19 Texas facilities with any disclosed power figure.

The published number is a single campus total covering SAT2 through SAT4. It is not broken down by building, no rack count is given, and no tenant is named. Any rack estimate is arithmetic on an assumed density, not an operator claim, and CyrusOne publishes no density of its own. The certifications, PCI DSS through TIA-942, qualify the campus for regulated workloads without revealing who occupies it.

The 36 MW matters because it is a real number in a state where most capacity is not. Texas has 137 mapped facilities, but only 19 publish a power figure, and those 19 total 475.41 MW. The fourth-place ranking rests on that small disclosed subset, not on the full state footprint, so the comparison understates what Texas actually holds.

What the data does not cover is the part that would explain the number: no expansion plans, no tenant, no density, no breakdown by building. The score of 68 reflects published IT capacity and operator type, and it flags announced expansion as missing. A reader can see that this campus is large and disclosed, and cannot see from this record how fully it is used or what it is used for.
